test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 14 Nov, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding festivals followed in Christianity?

A. Easter is the day celebrated for the ‘Resurrection of Jesus Christ’.

B. According to the Bible, ‘Three days after Jesus was crucified, he was resurrected’.

C. Good Friday is to commemorate the day of crucifixion of Jesus Christ.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3 (A, B and C)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Easter** is celebrated for the resurrection of Jesus Christ, an event that is central to Christian belief.
 
• According to the Bible, Jesus was resurrected three days after being crucified, an event that is commemorated as **Easter**.
 
• **Good Friday** is observed to remember the day Jesus Christ was crucified, marking his sacrifice for humanity.
 
• All the statements A, B, and C are correct regarding Christian festivals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Easter**

 
 
• It is the most important festival in the Christian calendar, celebrating the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead.
 
• It is observed on the first Sunday after the first full moon following the vernal equinox.
 
• The week preceding Easter is known as Holy Week, which includes Maundy Thursday (commemorating the Last Supper) and Good Friday (commemorating the crucifixion).
 
 
 
• **Good Friday**
 
 
• It is a Christian holiday commemorating the crucifixion of Jesus and his death at Calvary.
 
• It is observed during Holy Week as part of the Paschal Triduum on the Friday preceding Easter Sunday.
 
• It is also known as Holy Friday, Great Friday, Great and Holy Friday, and Black Friday.
 
 
 
• **Crucifixion of Jesus**
 
 
• Crucifixion is a method of capital punishment where the victim is tied or nailed to a large wooden cross and left to hang until death.
 
• According to the New Testament, Jesus was crucified, died, and was buried, and on the third day, he rose again from the dead.
 
• This event is central to Christian theology, symbolizing Jesus' sacrifice for humanity's sins and his victory over death.
 
 
 
• **Resurrection of Jesus**
 
 
• The resurrection of Jesus is the Christian belief that Jesus rose from the dead on the third day after his crucifixion.
 
• This event is commemorated on Easter Sunday and is the cornerstone of Christian faith, signifying hope and eternal life.
 
• It is described in the New Testament and is considered the foundation of Christian belief and theology.
